fx_note: HFL.NZ is a thin secondary NZX listing (NZD-quoted) of a UK primary-listed, GBP-reporting Jersey closed-end investment trust (LSE: HFEL). All fundamental data (NAV, dividends, premium/discount history) is GBP pence. current_price and all intrinsic_value/entry_price fields are reported in NZD (to match the NZX quote) by converting the GBP-derived valuation at the live GBPNZD rate. A parallel 'gbp' sub-object gives native pence figures for direct comparison against HFEL.L. Cross-check at valuation date: HFEL.L 264.0p implies an NZX-equivalent price of NZ$6.07 (264.0p / 100 * 2.2972), vs the actual NZX quote of NZ$6.01 -- a tight ~1% discount, so the NZX quote is judged fair/liquid enough to use directly. NZ holders receive no imputation/franking-equivalent credit on UK-sourced trust dividends and bear fully unhedged GBP/NZD translation risk stacked on top of the trust's own multi-currency (unhedged KRW/TWD/HKD/AUD/SGD/INR etc.) portfolio exposure; NZ FIF/FDR tax rules likely apply for most retail holders, a further drag on the practical dividend-growth thesis not modelled here.
valuation_philosophy: Henderson Far East Income is a Jersey-domiciled closed-end investment trust holding a concentrated Asia-Pacific dividend-equity portfolio (LSE: HFEL, NZX secondary: HFL). It is not an operating company: it has no revenue in the operating-company sense, no EBITDA, no capex, no working-capital cycle, and its 'operating cash flow' is portfolio income net of tax, not free cash flow available to a claimant on a business. A Gordon-growth FCF/WACC DCF is structurally invalid here and is NOT used (FreeCashFlow, EBITDA, OperatingIncome and OperatingCashFlow are all correctly NULL in the source Metrics CSV). Instead this model uses the NAV-per-share-compounding + exit-premium/discount + dividend-stream framework applied consistently to the other closed-end trusts in this research folder (BIT.NZ, AFI.NZ, FIH.U, FRFHF): project NAV per share forward at a scenario capital-growth rate net of the ~1.12% ongoing charge and the near-full-cover dividend payout, add the projected dividend stream, apply a scenario exit premium/discount to the year-5 NAV (the market-clearing metric for a trust is P/NAV, not an earnings multiple), and discount both streams at a Asia-Pacific-and-trust-specific cost of equity. THE CENTRAL INVESTMENT QUESTION: is the trust's market-leading ~10% headline dividend yield funded by capital erosion? The record says partly yes -- bare NAV per share fell from 337.76p (FY2016) to 223.32p (FY2025), a -4.5%/yr CAGR, even as the dividend was raised every year and dividend cover sat at or below 1.0x in multiple years (FY2023 cover 0.864x, funded from the distributable reserve; FY2025 cover 1.003x, still drawing a modest £1.5m from the revenue reserve). Set against that is the Company's own disclosed NAV TOTAL RETURN (dividends reinvested) of +80.9% cumulative over the same 10 years (+6.1%/yr compounded), which shows that a holder who reinvested distributions has still compounded a positive return -- the headline yield is a genuine cash return, but a meaningful share of it has structurally been capital being returned rather than fresh income, and a spending (non-reinvesting) holder has seen real capital erosion. H1-2026's sharp NAV rebound to 261.38p (a 23.3% six-month NAV total return driven overwhelmingly by a Korean semiconductor/'value-up' rally that lifted the South Korea portfolio weight from 12.6% to 24.2%) is treated as a favourable, non-repeatable window rather than a new steady state -- the base case anchors to a BLEND of the FY2025 year-end NAV (223.32p, the last full-cycle audited figure) and the H1-2026 actual (261.38p, the most recent published figure), weighted 55%/45% toward the more conservative FY2025 figure, rather than either extrapolating the H1-2026 peak forward or ignoring the real, published gain. The base case then assumes only modest (1%/yr) further NAV price growth -- consistent with the 9-year realised CAGR of -4.5% as a warning anchor against optimism, while acknowledging the post-FY2023 strategic pivot toward a blended value+growth portfolio (first positive capital return since 2017 in FY2025) provides some genuine reason for cautious improvement rather than continued outright decline. The base case correctly produces a MODEST NEGATIVE upside (-9.97%) at the current NZ$6.01 price, which sits at essentially par to the most recently published NAV (261.38p, +0.09% implied P/NAV) -- near the richest end of the trust's own 10-year premium/discount history (max +3.4%). This is not a manufactured bearish result: it follows directly from paying near-par for a NAV base that already embeds an unusually strong six-month rally, discounted at a cost of equity that reflects the trust's real structural risks (gearing, semiconductor concentration, key-person risk, NZX illiquidity, FX translation).

inputs.nav_h1_2026_asof: 2026-02-28 (H1 FY2026 half-year report, released 2026-04-14) -- most recent published NAV, no more current figure disclosed
inputs.nav_blend_methodology: Base-case starting NAV = 0.55 x FY2025 year-end NAV (223.32p, last full-cycle audited figure) + 0.45 x H1-2026 actual (261.38p, most recent published figure) = 240.45p. This deliberately does NOT extrapolate the H1-2026 Korean-semiconductor-rally peak forward as the new run-rate (per the analysis JSON's explicit warning), while still giving material weight to the real, published gain rather than ignoring it. See valuation_philosophy.
inputs.units: millions except per-share figures (pence) and NAV/price data
inputs.fcf_dcf_note: Not applicable -- see valuation_philosophy and the Analysis JSON's valuation_approach block. No FCF projection, WACC-Gordon terminal value, or SBC adjustment is used; those schema fields below are populated with null plus explanatory notes for schema consistency with operating-company DCFs, and are functionally replaced by the NAV-compounding equivalents.
inputs.sbc_source: unavailable -- not applicable to an externally-managed investment trust (Janus Henderson); no employees, no equity compensation scheme at the trust level
inputs.buyback_cash_note: HFL is a persistent NET ISSUER of shares (trading at a premium lets the Board issue accretively), the opposite of most sector peers; FY2025 saw 17.6m new shares issued raising £39.1m, and a further ~c.20.8m shares/£51.1m in and shortly after H1-2026. No buybacks were conducted despite AGM authority to do so (up to 14.99% of issued capital) -- authorized, not executed, so recorded as 0 per project convention.
inputs.shares_note: Share count is not projected as a per-share dilution/buyback mechanic (unlike an SBC-driven operating company) -- accretive issuance at a premium is NAV-per-share POSITIVE (adds net assets per share above the pre-issuance NAV) and is implicitly captured in the NAV-growth scenario assumptions rather than modelled as a separate share-count line.
inputs.net_debt_note: Gross bank loan £49.6m less cash £25.11m (H1-2026). This is short-term working-capital/gearing debt inside the investment vehicle's own capital structure, already reflected inside published NAV per share -- it is NOT subtracted again from the DCF output the way an operating company's net debt is subtracted from enterprise value, because NAV per share is already a per-share NET-of-debt figure.
inputs.fx_note: Fundamentals are GBP (Henderson Far East Income, London-listed HFEL.L, quoted in pence); HFL.NZ quotes NZD. Canonical weighted_iv is NZD to match the quote; weighted_iv_gbp_pence is the native London figure. NOTE pence, not pounds: the GBp series is 1/100 GBP.
inputs.currency_field_note: Normalized 2026-09-01 to a bare ISO code (was 'NZD (outputs) / GBP (fundamentals)'). The dual basis is now expressed by quote_currency + fx_note, not crammed into the code field. No valuation number changed.

historical_growth.methodology: HFL's own preferred value driver is NAV-per-share TOTAL RETURN (NAV growth + dividends paid), not revenue/EPS/equity CAGRs in the operating-company sense. Standard fields are shown below for schema completeness but are NOT the growth driver used in projections -- NetIncome/EPS for a trust is dominated by unrealised/realised capital-account gains and losses on the portfolio (e.g. FY2020 NetIncome -£48.8m, FY2021 +£29.7m) rather than an operating trend, and 'Revenue' in the CSV is investment income only.
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base_case_nav_price_growth_assumption (not a pure historical CAGR -- see notes)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Net-assets (equity) CAGR of +0.58%/yr over 9 years is NOT comparable to NAV-per-share CAGR of -4.49%/yr -- net assets grew (helped materially by accretive share issuance, shares outstanding roughly doubling from 114.5m FY2016 to 198.5m H1-2026) even as NAV PER SHARE fell, because the trust has been issuing new shares near/above NAV throughout most of the period. Revenue and EPS CAGRs are not meaningful for this ticker (income and NetIncome reflect portfolio yield and mark-to-market capital swings, not an operating trend) and are left null.
historical_growth.notes: The defining historical fact for HFL/HFEL is a PERSISTENT DECLINE in bare NAV per share (-4.5%/yr over 9 years, accelerating to -7.4%/yr over the most recent 3 years to FY2025) occurring simultaneously with an 18-consecutive-year DIVIDEND INCREASE STREAK and dividend cover hovering at or just below 1.0x -- the clearest possible signature of a high yield partly funded by capital return rather than fresh income. Set against this, the Company's own disclosed NAV TOTAL RETURN (dividends reinvested) of +80.9% cumulative (+6.1%/yr) over the same 10 years shows the total economic return to a reinvesting holder has still been positive, just meaningfully below both a typical global-equity benchmark and the sector average (per the Analysis JSON, HFEL has trailed the AIC Asia Pacific Equity Income sector average across every measured horizon to Aug-2026: 1yr 23.6% vs sector 40.7%; 3yr 50.5% vs 83.2%; 5yr 35.1% vs 72.6%; 10yr 72.1% vs 174.9%). H1-2026's +23.3% NAV total return (Korean semiconductor/'value-up' rally) is the sharpest positive outlier in the series and is explicitly NOT extrapolated as a new run-rate in the base case.

base.rationale: NAV price growth of just +1.0%/yr is deliberately modest and anchored against the realised -4.5%/yr 9-year decline as a warning signal, while acknowledging the post-FY2023 strategic pivot toward a blended value+growth portfolio has delivered the first positive capital return per share since 2017 (FY2025: +1.42p) and could sustain small positive NAV price appreciation net of the 1.12% ongoing charge and near-full dividend payout. Dividend growth of 0.8%/yr matches the pace of the FY2026 declared interims (+0.8% YoY) rather than assuming the streak accelerates. Exit premium/discount of 0.0% (par to NAV) reflects the trust's persistent tendency to trade at a small premium (8 of the last 10 years) without assuming that premium expands from today's level.

bull.rationale: Asia-wide governance/dividend reform (Korea 'value-up', China SOE payout push, broader regional reform) and the AI/semiconductor supply-chain leadership theme persist, the post-FY2023 strategic rebalancing continues to deliver (as in H1-2026), and the trust sustains a modest premium supported by continued index inclusion (FTSE 250 from April 2026) and yield-hungry retail demand enabling further accretive issuance. NAV price growth of +6%/yr is well below the H1-2026 annualised pace but materially better than the historical realised average.

bear.rationale: The realised 9-year NAV decline of -4.5%/yr resumes/persists as the Korean semiconductor rally that drove H1-2026 unwinds (management itself flagged a Feb-2026 'sharp sell-off in Asian software stocks' on AI-disruption fears, and warned of 'more to come'), the sector/manager-relative underperformance documented in the Analysis JSON continues, and ~12% gross gearing amplifies the drawdown. Dividend cover (already below 1.0x in FY2023 and only marginally above in FY2025/H1-2026) breaks decisively, forcing a one-off 15% dividend cut in Year 2 followed by continued shrinkage, consistent with the trust having explicitly drawn on distributable/revenue reserves in multiple recent years even in a reasonable income year. The persistent premium -- unusual in the sector and the trust's key structural advantage -- reverses to a -10% discount (in line with peers, most of which already trade at a discount), closing off the accretive-issuance engine and removing the capital-raising tailwind.

base.implied_exit_multiple: n/a -- trust valuation uses P/NAV, not an earnings multiple

entry_price.methodology: Price today such that 5 years of projected BASE-CASE dividends plus the year-5 exit value (year-5 NAV x base-case 0% exit premium/discount, i.e. par to NAV) discounted at a 15% hurdle equals that price. Uses base-case cashflows only, per project methodology.
entry_price.memo: A 15% IRR hurdle applied to a trust whose base-case total return (dividend yield ~10% plus modest NAV growth) is roughly 11-13% p.a. requires paying a meaningful discount to today's price -- NZ$4.85 (GBp 211.3), a -19.2% implied discount to the most recent published NAV (261.38p) and -12.2% below the blended starting NAV used for the base case. This sits within, but toward the wider end of, HFL's own 10-year premium/discount range (+3.4% to -1.9%), so unlike some trusts in this repo where the 15% hurdle demands an unprecedented discount, this entry level is a plausible (if currently unavailable) buy point rather than a purely theoretical one. It should be read as 'the price at which HFL becomes an attractive 15%-IRR holding', not as a near-term price target.

sanity_check.description: For an investment trust the natural sanity anchor is price/NAV (P/NAV), not P/E or EV/EBITDA -- both are set to null because reported NetIncome is dominated by unrealised mark-to-market capital-account swings and there is no EBITDA concept for a portfolio of listed securities. Trip test: does the implied P/NAV at the base-case IV exceed the 10-year maximum premium (+3.4%) by more than 1.5x, or is the model extrapolating the H1-2026 NAV peak? Neither condition is met: the base-case IV (235.54p) is BELOW the H1-2026 NAV (261.38p) and below the blended starting NAV (240.45p) -- i.e. the model output already reflects capital erosion and a below-par exit multiple, the opposite of extrapolating the peak. The base-case implied P/NAV at the base-case exit (0%, par) is within the trust's own 10-year range (-1.9% to +3.4%).

implied_multiples.price_to_earnings: n/a -- NetIncome is dominated by mark-to-market capital-account gains/losses, not an operating earnings concept
implied_multiples.ev_to_ebitda: n/a -- no EBITDA concept for a portfolio of listed securities; no capex/working-capital cycle

sanity_check.peak_extrapolation_check: PASS -- the base-case starting NAV (240.45p, blended) is materially BELOW the most recent H1-2026 NAV (261.38p), and the base-case intrinsic value (235.54p) is below both. The model explicitly discounts the H1-2026 peak rather than extrapolating it forward; see valuation_philosophy and nav_blend_methodology.
sanity_check.diagnosis: The current market price (implied 261.62p, essentially the H1-2026 NAV) sits at the richest end of HFL's own 10-year premium/discount history (max recorded premium +3.4%, current implied premium to the most recent NAV effectively 0%, but +8.8% to the more conservative blended NAV this model uses as its base-case anchor and +17.1% to the last full-cycle audited FY2025 NAV). This is the primary source of the base case's negative upside: the market is pricing HFL as if the H1-2026 semiconductor-rally NAV level is durable, while the model treats it as a favourable but partly transient six-month window. None of the three DCF scenarios themselves breach the trust's historical P/NAV range at their respective exit multiples (bear -10%, base 0%, bull +5%, all within or adjacent to the 10-year -1.9%/+3.4% range), so the check passes by construction.
sanity_check.fix_applied: None required -- no scenario individually breaches the historical range or extrapolates the NAV peak. The negative base-case upside is a legitimate output of paying a price close to a cyclically elevated NAV, not a modelling artefact; see valuation_philosophy for why this is reported as-is rather than adjusted.

sensitivity.methodology: 5-year build fair value (PV of dividends + PV of exit value at year-5 NAV x column exit premium/discount, both discounted at the row cost of equity), holding base-case NAV price growth (+1.0%/yr) and dividend growth (+0.8%/yr) constant, in GBP pence and NZD (at GBPNZD 2.2972). Row/column labels follow this ticker's actual value drivers (cost of equity and exit premium/discount) rather than the generic WACC/terminal-growth schema field names, which are reused here for dashboard compatibility.

probability_weighted.weighted_iv_currency_note: weighted_iv is stated in NZD to match the HFL.NZ quote currency used by the screener; weighted_iv_gbp_pence is the native London (HFEL.L) figure in pence.

cost_of_equity_build.methodology: Built up from a UK gilt risk-free rate plus named risk premia specific to this ticker, rather than a CAPM beta regression (a closed-end trust's observed beta is distorted by its own premium/discount volatility, which is a separate risk already captured in the exit-multiple scenario range).
cost_of_equity_build.gearing_premium_rationale: ~12% gross / ~6% net gearing on the £50m RBSi revolving credit facility amplifies both gains and losses; facility renews only every ~24 months (expires Aug-2027), creating periodic refinancing/repricing risk.
cost_of_equity_build.concentration_premium_rationale: Portfolio rotated sharply toward Korean/Taiwanese semiconductors (South Korea 12.6%->24.2%, Technology 24.4%->25.4% of the portfolio between Aug-2025 and Feb-2026), trading one concentration risk (deep-value/high-yield underperformance) for another (AI capex-cycle and memory-chip pricing risk); management itself flagged a Feb-2026 Asian-software sell-off as evidence this risk is already live.
cost_of_equity_build.key_person_premium_rationale: Long-serving co-manager Mike Kerley retired from the industry in mid-2024, leaving Sat Duhra as sole named lead manager of a ~£400-500m portfolio; the second experienced voice/counterweight is gone.
cost_of_equity_build.illiquidity_premium_rationale: HFL.NZ is a small, comparatively illiquid NZX secondary line versus the LSE-listed HFEL, with wider bid/ask spreads and less efficient price discovery for NZ holders.
cost_of_equity_build.bull_bear_rationale: Bull case uses a lower CoE (11%) reflecting reduced concentration/key-person stress if the post-FY2023 strategic pivot continues to succeed; bear case uses a higher CoE (13%) reflecting the concentration and gearing risks fully crystallising alongside a wider exit discount.
cost_of_equity_build.fx_translation_note: No separate additive FX premium is applied to the discount rate for the NZD-quoted output (consistent with the BIT.NZ precedent in this repo) -- GBP/NZD translation risk for the NZ investor is instead captured qualitatively in the fx_note and left to the reader's own currency view, since adding a currency risk premium to a real-asset discount rate conflates two different sources of variance.
